title: Racing the deadline
description: An app gives a request 300 ms. The request first waits in a busy gateway, then fans out to two services. Compare what happens when the gateway ignores the deadline (Before) with what happens when it passes the remaining time on (After).

atRest.caption: Press Play to watch the request from the start.

intro.caption: The App sets its stopwatch. First 200 ms: the time the Gateway may spend on its own work.
Then 100 ms more: a safety buffer on top.
300 ms in total. The App presses start and sends the request.

moments.caption: The request leaves the App. Its deadline is 300 ms away, and the countdown starts.
The Gateway is busy, so the request waits in its queue. The countdown keeps running.
At 200 ms the Gateway asks Services A and B. Only 100 ms are left.
Before: each service gets the full 200 ms timeout, so B could run until 400 ms, long after the deadline.
After: the Gateway passes the deadline on. 100 ms are left, minus a 20 ms reserve, so each service gets 80 ms.
Service A answers in 20 ms. Its reply waits in the Gateway, which sends one combined answer.
Service B's 80 ms run out. The Gateway marks B as timed out and builds the answer.
The answer with A's reply reaches the App before 300 ms. A's work is used.
300 ms: the deadline passes. The App stops waiting, cancels the call, and A's reply is lost.
